title: Practice 5: Genitive endings: nouns, adjectives, pronouns

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Эта земля покрыта зелёным ковром из ___ (пышный) растительности.
exercises.prompt: This land is covered by a verdant carpet of lush vegetation.
exercises.why: Similarly, feminine adjectives in the genitive case have the same ending as the prepositional case: **-ой**, or, after the same five 'hush' consonants, **-ей**. *Кило́ хоро́шего ру́сского сы́ра Кило́ хоро́шей ру́сской колбасы́* — From the Wikibooks Russian textbook (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 46.
exercises.context: Similarly, feminine adjectives in the genitive case have the same ending as the prepositional case: **-ой**, or, after the same five 'hush' consonants, **-ей**.

exercises.prompt: Tom wakes from a deep sleep.
exercises.why: Like nouns, masculine and neuter adjectives have the same ending in the genitive singular, **-ого**, pronounced 'oh-vo'. — From the Wikibooks Russian textbook (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 46.
exercises.context: Like nouns, masculine and neuter adjectives have the same ending in the genitive singular, **-ого**, pronounced 'oh-vo'.

exercises.prompt: Talking on and on won't make the pot boil.
exercises.why: However, there is a peculiarity in Russian when counting: though we use the genitive singular on nouns that are numbered 2, 3, 4, 22, 23, 24, etc, we use the genitive *plural* for any adjectives attached to that noun: *Три кни́жных магази́на Пять книжных магази́нов Он зна́ет сто два ру́сских сло́ва Он зна́ет сто шесть ру́сских слов* — From the Wikibooks Russian textbook (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 46.
